Long story short, some lobbyists want to remove the Safe Harbor provision from the DMCA. In practice, this will likely lead to websites being legally required to essentially monitor and filter everything, or remove the ability of users to post outright, while corporations abuse it to silence people they don't like. They're already doing it, in fact, and this gives them a lot more reach to make it worse.

Original request for comments, plus background information: https://www.federalregister.gov/articles/2015/12/31/2015-32973/section-512-study-notice-and-request-for-public-comment

Extension to request for comments: https://www.regulations.gov/#!documentDetail;D=COLC-2015-0013-0002

EFF Analysis: https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2016/01/notice-and-stay-down-really-filter-everything

Form letter: https://www.takedownabuse.org/#save-fair-use
DMCA Safe Harbor in Jeopardy, May Result In Filtering - Comment to the Copyright Office before April 1, 11:59 PM Eastern

Safe Harbor is literally the only aspect of the DMCA that's good for anyone but the copyright lobby. It was the trade off that allowed the rest to be passed without massive opposition from tech firms.

If DMCA safe harbor gets taken out then we are truly screwed.
So are we leaving personal comments in the comments section when we request for comments?

Depends on what you mean by personal comments.

If you have any specific thoughts on the subject, particularly well-reasoned ones that are thought out, yes. If you have only a couple sentences that aren't very coherent, you would probably do better using the form letter. Note I say probably - they say in the guidelines that one well-written comment can be more powerful than a thousand form letters. But given the quality of some of the comments the FCC got regarding Net Neutrality, I can't help but think some of those might have done better as a form letter.

If you need more of a guide, search for "Subjects of Inquiry" on the first link. They have about 30 specific questions to help with.
